title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X and Y are 'anabelian' topological surfaces of finite type (compact surfaces minus finitely many points, with negative Euler characteristic). A_X is the homeomorphism group of X, and A°_X is the subgroup of homeomorphisms isotopic to the identity.

(1) End of the proof of the Corollary from the previous page. Claim: every isotopy class of finite étale maps (finite unbranched covers) X→Y is a right torsor under A°_X.
- Prop. 1 gives transitivity: two isotopic covering maps differ by precomposition with an element of A°_X.
- Freeness remains. Suppose u∈A°_X satisfies f∘u=f. Then u is a deck transformation of X over Y that is isotopic to the identity.
- Prop. 2 (previous page) says such a u is the identity. Modern argument: a nontrivial deck transformation acts freely. A map homotopic to the identity has Lefschetz number χ(X)≠0, so it has a fixed point. Hence u=id.

(2) Corollary 2. The connected components of the space of finite étale maps X→Y are contractible. Each component is an A°_X-torsor, hence homeomorphic to A°_X = Homeo_0(X), which is contractible for hyperbolic surfaces (Hamstrom; Earle–Eells).

(3) Corollary 3. Consider the extended (non-oriented) Teichmüller modular group T_X = A_X/A°_X, i.e. the extended mapping class group. It acts by precomposition on Hom_isot(X,Y), the set of isotopy classes of finite étale maps X→Y.
- Stabilizers: the stabilizer of [f] is identified with the deck group Aut_Y(X) of the cover Y'_f defined by f. It injects into T_X by Prop. 2, so it is finite.
- Orbits: the orbits correspond bijectively to R_X(Y), the set of isomorphism classes of finite étale covers of Y homeomorphic to X.
- Oriented version: under T_X^+ the orbits are R_X(Y)×{±1}, the sign recording whether f preserves or reverses orientation.

Margin notes:
- First note: apparently 'every finite subgroup of T_X comes from a finite group of automorphisms ... !!', i.e. a statement or question of Nielsen realization type.
- Second note: 'this set of orbits is finite'. The degree is fixed by χ(X)=d·χ(Y), and Y has finitely many covers of each degree.

Purpose: this sets up the next page. There, surfaces with isotopy classes of orientation-preserving finite étale maps form an 'isotopic category'. Its Hom-sets are then profinitely completed (Hom^ = Hom ×^{Γ_X} Γ̂_X) to get a category on which Gal(Q̄/Q) should act. This is the Teichmüller tower / profinite Teichmüller groupoid program.
errors: No mathematical errors. Corollary 2 implicitly needs that the continuous bijection A°_X → component (u ↦ f∘u) is a homeomorphism in the compact-open topology, and that Homeo_0 is contractible also for punctured (non-compact, finite type) surfaces. Both are true but unstated.

The margin NB about finite subgroups of T_X does not follow from the page. The stabilizers produced here are only the deck groups of free actions. The general statement (Nielsen realization) is a deep theorem (Kerckhoff 1980/83), and the realizing action is generally not free.

ideas.what: Isotopy classes of finite covering maps X→Y are free and transitive A°_X-orbits; a deck transformation isotopic to the identity is trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of periodic mapping classes / freeness of the Homeo_0 action on covering maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Nielsen, Lefschetz fixed-point argument; Birman–Hilden context)

ideas.what: Components of the space of finite étale maps between hyperbolic surfaces are contractible.
ideas.modern_name: Contractibility of Homeo_0 / Diff_0 of hyperbolic surfaces

ideas.what: Action of the extended mapping class group on isotopy classes of covers: stabilizer is the deck group, orbits are iso classes of covers, orbit set finite, orientation sign splitting.
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group action on finite covers / characteristic subgroup counting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (via Dehn–Nielsen–Baer, outer automorphisms acting on finite-index subgroups)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower), not this formulation

ideas.what: Margin: every finite subgroup of T_X is induced by a finite group of homeomorphisms.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nielsen (problem), Kerckhoff 1980/1983 (solution); Fenchel, Zieschang for special cases

missed.claim: Grothendieck, around 1978–80, flags the Nielsen realization statement in a marginal note with '!!'. This is roughly contemporaneous with Kerckhoff's solution, and in the context of finite stabilizers of the Teichmüller group acting on covers. Historically interesting as evidence of his awareness, but not new mathematics.
missed.quote: NB Tout sous-groupe fini de T_X provient ... d'un groupe fini d'automorphismes ... !!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor historical datum linking the Galois–Teichmüller program to Nielsen realization, i.e. finite-order elements of profinite mapping class groups. Profinite analogues of Nielsen realization remain partially open.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of standard foundational facts on isotopy classes of finite covers of hyperbolic surfaces and the mapping class group action, preparing the profinite isotopic category. The only notable detail is the marginal Nielsen-realization remark, which is known mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The set is written Hom_isot(X,Y) ('isot' as subscript) and called 'morphismes isotopiques', not 'Hom_ext' / 'morphismes extérieurs'.
The struck-out start of Corollaire 3 reads 'L'ensemble Hom_isot(X,Y) est'. The replacement is 'L'opération induite des ... groupe de Teichmüller'.
First margin note likely reads roughly: 'NB Tout sous-groupe fini de T_X provient-il d'un groupe fini d'automorphismes [de X] ?!!'. Uncertain whether it is a question or an assertion.
Second margin note: 'NB cet ens d'orbites est fini !'.
The page number at the bottom left is 7.
